name: Genetic Congenital Limb Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Congenital Limb Malformations

criteria.description: Presence of congenital limb malformation affecting one or more limbs
Positive family history of similar limb malformations consistent with genetic inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in known limb development genes
Radiographic evidence of bone and joint anomalies consistent with congenital limb malformation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital limb malformation with either positive family history or pathogenic genetic variant identified
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by genetic testing and imaging studies.

pathognomonic.notes: Absence or hypoplasia of bones along the long axis of the limb
Fusion of two or more digits

common.notes: Shortening of the fingers or toes
Permanent flexion contracture of one or more fingers
Limited range of motion due to soft tissue or joint abnormalities
Underdevelopment of muscles in affected limbs
searchTerms: small or weak muscles in limbs

occasional.notes: Split hand or split foot malformation
Curvature of a digit in the plane of the palm
Underdeveloped or absent nails on affected digits

rare.notes: Rarely co-occurs with congenital heart defects
Occasional sensorineural or conductive hearing loss
Mild facial anomalies in some genetic syndromes

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing mutations in limb development genes (e.g., HOXD13, GLI3, TBX5)
imaging: X-ray showing bone hypoplasia, aplasia, or abnormal digit formation
MRI for soft tissue and muscle assessment
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes regulating limb morphogenesis
Autosomal dominant or recessive inheritance patterns depending on subtype
other: Family history consistent with hereditary limb malformations
Prenatal ultrasound may detect limb anomalies

distinguishingFeatures: Complete absence of one or more limbs rather than partial malformations
Typically isolated limb absence without syndactyly or polydactyly
Hematological abnormalities not present in isolated genetic limb malformations

redFlags: Severe limb deformities incompatible with function
Presence of associated systemic anomalies (e.g., cardiac defects)
Family history of syndromic limb malformations requiring genetic counseling
references: Orphanet: Genetic congenital limb malformation - ORPHA:183536
